text:
jonathan: Heads-up — saw a reproduction of the continuous-batching OOM on dedicated-ci while testing seq-length mix (short + very long). attaching perf notes below.

maria: thanks — short summary?

jonathan: short: when batch growth spikes (we hit a 2x increase in live sequences across the epoch) the slab allocator refuses to shrink fast enough, workspace peak grows, then the KV cache reclaim path races with the allocator and we OOM. reproduced on 80G A100.

kai: is this the same as the earlier pad-estimate mismatch or a separate fragmentation issue?

jonathan: different surface. padding is still wasteful but main problem is allocator->free lag + deferred frees held by streams. plus we observed a per-seq ephemeral tensor that is allocated per request kernel switch (approx 1.2MB/seq) that isn't reused across batches.

tara: can you paste the short log & pprof snapshot?

jonathan: sure. excerpt:
```
[2026-03-15 14:02:13] batch_size=96 -> 188 (growth)
GPU memory used: 41.2G -> 65.8G in ~2s
alloc slab: arena0: 58G reserved, 12G in free-cache
OOM at step 14321: cudaMalloc failed (out of memory)
backtrace: allocator::alloc_workspace -> kernel_launch -> service_thread
KV cache evict triggered: evicted 3 chunks (24MB) but unable to reclaim slab pages
```

eli: interesting the KV evict only freed tiny amounts vs slab pressure. looks like fragmentation + reserve policy.

alloc-bot: alloc-metrics: peak_live_buffers=1432, per_seq_temp_avg=1.18MB, free_list_frag=18%

maria: hypothesis: deferred free by in-flight CUDA streams holds large allocations, so even after eviction we still can't coalesce. also our per-request kill-switch for prefetched KV isn't synchronous.

jonathan: exactly. also kernel selection matters: some fused kernels we pick allocate their own temporaries (gemm buffers) per-batch which blow the working set when sequences vary.

kai: proposals?

jonathan: 1) opportunistic slab shrink: introduce an epoch-based shrink that runs when batch growth > threshold. shrink uses cudaMemAdvise or cudaFreeAsync on a dedicated stream and waits at a safe point (end of step) to avoid racing kernels.

jonathan: 2) per-seq temp pooling: track per-seq ephemeral buffer shapes and keep a small LRU pool keyed by (seq_len_bucket, dtype). reuse before new alloc. caps to X MB per-GPU to avoid unbounded retention.

tara: 3) KV cooperative reclaim: when slab pressure is high, force synchronous KV eviction path (sync free) for >Y bytes instead of async path. cost: a small sync stall but avoids OOM.

eli: 4) kernel selection hinting: when variance in seq-length within batch is high, bias towards kernels that use fewer temporaries even if slightly slower. needs perf model to decide tradeoff.

maria: all sound good. any quick wins to reduce OOM risk for customers?

jonathan: short-term: (a) cap automatic batch growth (growth factor 1.3 instead of 2.0 when history shows slab_util>70%) (b) enable per-seq pooling default in dedicated builds (cheap to add)

kai: medium-term: implement epoch shrink + KV sync for critical paths. need benchmarks: how much latency p99 added by sync eviction?

jonathan: ran microbenchmarks: sync eviction of 200MB adds ~6ms median, ~20ms p99 in our harness (dominated by cudaFree sync). but it prevents 300MB OOM trains in busy hosts.

tara: can we instead expose a reclaim token to request path so requests can declare short-lived buffers that allocator can reuse immediately? like annotated allocations.

eli: yes, annotations are nice but more invasive. per-seq pooling achieves similar benefit with less intrusive changes.

maria: who will prototype?

jonathan: i'll prototype per-seq pooling + cap-growth toggle. kai can take epoch shrink + kernel hinting. tara/eli take KV sync path and eval latencies.

kai: timeline? PRs next week?

jonathan: i'll have an initial PR by Tue with a simple LRU pool (config flags: per_seq_pool_enabled, per_seq_pool_cap_mb). will add tests: high variance replay + assert no OOMs.

alloc-bot: TODO created: ALLOC-1720 implement per-seq pool (assignee: jonathan)

maria: nice. also add telemetry: per_seq_temp_reuse_rate, slab_shrink_runs, forced_kv_sync_count so ops can see behavior.

jonathan: agreed. will wire metrics.

tara: if anyone hits this in staging, set env REDWOOD_BATCH_GROWTH_MAX=1.2 as hotfix.

eli: thanks all — good catch. this explains some customer OOMs last week that looked random.

maria: closing loop: once jonathan's PR lands, we'll run e2e replay for 48h on dedicated-ci with mixed seq profiles and report.

jonathan: updated plan in PR description when ready. :rocket:
